title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the 'algebraic group scheme' variation inside 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the continuation of La Longue Marche. Grothendieck mimics the Teichmüller-tower objects of genus 0 (M_{0,3}, the profinite group \hat{\mathfrak G}_{0,3}, T^!_{0,3}, etc.) with linear group schemes over a base S. The input is a pair (ρ,σ) of elements of SG = SL(2)_S. In the 'cas modulaire' of the next page, ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] (order 6) and σ = [[0,1],[-1,0]] (order 4). These are the standard generators of SL_2(Z) ≅ Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6, the discrete shadow of π_1 of the modular orbifold and of M_{0,3}-type data.

Objects from the previous pages. T_ρ is the torus centralising ρ and N'_σ is (a variant of) the normaliser of the torus of σ. G*_{ρ,σ}(0) ⊂ T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, and M_{ρ,σ} := G*_{ρ,σ}(0)·SG. The structure established so far:
- (20): M_{ρ,σ} is an extension of μ_2×μ_2 by M^0_{ρ,σ}.
- (22): ST_ρ × ST_σ is central in M^0_{ρ,σ}, with quotient G.
- (23)/(24): M^{0+}_{ρ,σ} = Ker(χ: M^0 → G_m) ≅ ST_ρ × ST_σ × SG.
- (25): there is a canonical μ_2^3 ↪ M^{0+}.

This page.
- (26): the μ_2^3 of (25) comes from the canonical central inclusions μ_2 ↪ ST_ρ, μ_2 ↪ ST_σ and μ_2 ↪ SG (the last via -I).
- (27): this gives canonical global sections, Σ = (Z/2)^3 → Γ(M^{0+}_{ρ,σ}) ⊂ Γ(M^*_{ρ,σ}).
- He then introduces a dictionary of notation 'paraphrasing' the M_{0,3} notation. The normal subgroup SG is renamed 𝔊^+_{ρ,σ}, the analogue of \hat{\mathfrak G}^+_{0,3} (the profinite fundamental group of the thrice-punctured sphere). The quotient is T^!_{ρ,σ} := M_{ρ,σ}/𝔊^+_{ρ,σ} (28), the analogue of T^!_{0,3}, the 'Teichmüller' outer part.
- (29): T^!_{ρ,σ} ≅ SG*_{ρ,σ}(ω), embedded in T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ. He announces the simpler notation T_{ρ,σ}.
- (30)/(31): the exact sequence 1 → SL(2) → M_{ρ,σ} → T^!_{ρ,σ} → 1 splits canonically as a semidirect product, M_{ρ,σ} ≅ M_{ρ,σ}(ω) ⋉ 𝔊^+_{ρ,σ}.
- The dark-ink marginal note is a later self-correction. It warns about rigour or notation for (28)/(29) and says that the 'paraphrase' into group schemes should be done more carefully, with a different letter.

Purpose. The aim is to build an algebraic (group-scheme) model of the pair 'fundamental group ⊂ Teichmüller/automorphism group' for M_{0,3}, with SL(2) replacing the profinite free group. The loop equation and the M_{0,3}/M_{0,4} formalism can then be studied in a linear-algebraic setting. The next page shows the analogy breaking down: SL(2) is connected, so no S_3-quotient exists. It also shows that, in the modular case, there is a canonical section τ_∞ = diag(-1,1).
errors: Notation is unstable on this page: T^!_{ρ,σ}, T_{ρ,σ} and SG*_{ρ,σ}(ω) are all used for the quotient, and M^* versus M^{0+} appear in (27). The marginal note itself flags the notation of (28)/(29) as needing more rigour or revision.

The semidirect splitting (31) is asserted, not proved. It requires M_{ρ,σ}(ω) ∩ SG = 1, i.e. that SG*_{ρ,σ}(ω) maps isomorphically to the quotient. This is plausible from the construction on earlier pages but not checked here.

The injectivity of μ_2^3 → M^{0+} relies on the product decomposition (24). Inside M_{ρ,σ} as a subgroup of T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ·SG, the centres -I could a priori coincide; the decomposition (24) is what guarantees independence.

ideas.what: Canonical (Z/2)^3 of central involutions coming from the centres μ_2 of ST_ρ, ST_σ and SL(2)
ideas.modern_name: centre of SL_2 and of maximal tori; elementary abelian 2-subgroup of central elements

ideas.what: Group-scheme analogue of the M_{0,3} Teichmüller data: SL(2) plays the role of \hat{\mathfrak G}^+_{0,3}, with an 'outer' quotient T^!_{ρ,σ} built from tori and normalisers attached to a pair (ρ,σ) of elements (in the modular case, generators of SL_2(Z))
ideas.modern_name: algebraic/linear model of the automorphism tower of π_1(P^1 - 3 points); compare relative completions/Malcev-type algebraic envelopes of SL_2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart; the related relative completion of SL_2(Z) is due to Hain (1990s–2000s)

ideas.what: Canonical semidirect product splitting M_{ρ,σ} ≅ M_{ρ,σ}(ω) ⋉ SL(2)
ideas.modern_name: split extension of a group scheme by SL_2

missed.claim: A systematic 'paraphrase' of the genus-0 Teichmüller formalism (M_{0,3}, 𝔊^+, T^!) into the category of group schemes over a base S, attached to a pair (ρ,σ) in SL(2). The modular case corresponds to the generators of SL_2(Z). The programme is begun here but visibly unsettled, as the marginal self-criticism and the failure of the S_3-quotient on the next page show.
missed.quote: Je vais introduire au sujet des groupes M_{ρ,σ} des notations qui paraphrasent les notations M_{0,3} etc, dans le contexte des schémas en groupes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates a linear-algebraic shadow of the Galois/GT action on π_1 of M_{0,3} and on SL_2(Z). This is loosely parallel to later work on relative completion of SL_2(Z) and on modular/elliptic motives (Hain, Brown, Enriquez's elliptic associators). It does not seem to have been developed in this form in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly notation and routine structure: central μ_2's, an exact sequence and a split extension. Its interest is the unusual programme of modelling the M_{0,3} Teichmüller data by group schemes built from SL(2) and a pair (ρ,σ). That programme is an unpublished direction, but this page contains no striking finished result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 likely reads 'donnant naissance à des sections canoniques' or similar ('liens' is doubtful); the next line is largely illegible.
'et une scindage canonique' should be 'et un scindage canonique'.
'sera utilisée de préférence : SG*_{ρ,σ}(ω)' likely means 'de préférence à SG*_{ρ,σ}(ω)'.
In (27) the right-hand group appears to be Γ M^*_{ρ,σ}, with a star superscript, containing Γ M^{0+}_{ρ,σ}.

The marginal note (dark ink) is only partially legible. It begins roughly 'Vu un peu trop maintenant la rigueur !' and mentions (28), (29) and a change of notation for T_{ρ,σ}, to 'paraphraser … en groupes'. The proposed letter appears to be 𝒯 rather than Γ.
